newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Gold slumped to its lowst level in more than three years, closing at $360.80 an ounce in New York on Friday and recovering only marginally to just more than $361 in Hong Kong on Saturday as investors took a negative view of the metal in a thin market.
- Two men were arrested at a police roadblock and appeared in court after several bombs exploded in and near Rustenburg, injuring several people.

- The Inkatha Freedom Party welcomed proposals for a peace package for KwaZulu-Natal, amid concern from other political parties that elements within the ANC might not be supportive if it includes a special amnesty deal.

- The Johannesburg Stock Exchnage saw a record year in 1996 in terms of turnover, capital raised and foreign involvement, but it was not a banner year in terms of the performance of the major indices.

- Overall performance in the manufacturing sector might stabilise next year with strong prospects for a bottoming out of the unfavourable conditions in the past few months, Stellenbosch University's Bureau for Economic Research said in its December survey.
- Police achieved an early breakthrough in Sunday's Rustenburg bombings when two right-wing suspects were arrested at a roadblock and they have vowed to crack down hard on all forms of terrorism.
